module_title: Basics of Plant Kingdom and Vascular Tissues
introduction: The Plant Kingdom consists of multicellular, eukaryotic, and autotrophic organisms. At this level, we divide the plant kingdom into basic categories and understand the 'plumbing system' that keeps them alive.

core_concepts.title: Broad Classification of Plants
core_concepts.description:
1. Cryptogams (Seedless Plants): Lower plants that do not produce flowers or seeds. They reproduce via 'spores'. (Examples: Algae, Mosses, Ferns). 
2. Phanerogams (Seed-Bearing Plants): Higher plants that produce seeds. (Examples: Pine trees, Mango trees, Rose bushes).

core_concepts.title: Vascular Tissues (The Plumbing System)
core_concepts.description:
Plants need a transport system to move water from roots and food from leaves. 
1. Xylem: Transports 'Water and Minerals' from the roots to the rest of the plant. 
2. Phloem: Transports 'Food' (prepared in the leaves by photosynthesis) to all other parts of the plant.

core_concepts.title: Photosynthesis (Basic)
core_concepts.description:
The process by which green plants make their own food using Sunlight, Carbon Dioxide ($CO_2$), and Water ($H_2O$) in the presence of Chlorophyll. 
Equation: $6CO_2 + 6H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight/Chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 \text{ (Glucose)} + 6O_2 \text{ (Oxygen)}$.

important_entities.name: Direction of Transport
important_entities.significance: Xylem transport is strictly 'Unidirectional' (only moves UP from roots to leaves). Phloem transport is 'Bidirectional' (moves both UP and DOWN depending on where the food is needed).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Because fungi (like mushrooms) grow in the soil, students often think they belong to the Plant Kingdom. They DO NOT. Fungi are heterotrophic (they don't have chlorophyll and can't make food) and belong to their own separate kingdom.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the sounds: Xylem transports 'Jal' (Water). Phloem transports 'Phal' (Food/Fruit).

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed question in SSC/Railways: 'Which tissue is responsible for the transport of food in plants?' Answer: Phloem.
